answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, with transition mass attenuated across each edge. A Sybil cluster separated by a sparse external cut has low conductance, so only limited walk probability can enter it; conductance inequalities and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap its aggregate voting weight, regardless of internal density. Thus glacier, trellis, and ember attestations cannot amplify collusion without earning costly external trust.
